lastTask: Cleanup pass: trim boilerplate, fix dry-run npm cache gate, improve summary/logging (Windows & Linux)
decisions: Windows providers call Invoke-Step with named parameters; the $params splat blocks were noise and shared mutable state.
Add-StepResult is the single place a result row is built; the unused Error field was removed on both scripts (Message already carries the error text).
Linux exposes LAST_STATUS from run_step so follow-up steps gate on the recorded result instead of $? or RESULTS string parsing.
run_step still returns 0 only on success; its comment documents that skipped/dry-run return 1.
npm cache runs when the npm row is Success or DryRun on both scripts, so --dry-run previews it and a failed/skipped npm never triggers it.
Invalid CLI args exit 2 (usage error). PowerShell rejects unknown parameters at binding time instead.
risks: No PowerShell runtime in this environment: Update-Windows.ps1 was reviewed statically (brace balance, backtick EOL, call-site arity, no leftover $params/Error refs) but not executed.
Windows elevation heuristic (prefix under $env:ProgramFiles) may skip npm for a rare user who can write there without elevation.
Removing the Test-Command guards means a machine without WSL now shows four WSL rows marked Skipped instead of none (more visible, not a regression).
nextActions: Commit and push the cleanup pass (pending user confirmation).
Run Update-Windows.ps1 -DryRun once on a Windows machine to confirm the split provider calls bind correctly.
